architecture.A1 System context: Local desktop human, Agent caller and generic-run caller request DispatchHost; only DispatchHost may reach EXEC. Current trusted approval actor/source: NOT ESTABLISHED. spec_approve is a local command, not a separately authenticated human authority.
architecture.A2 Hexagonal system view: See diagram A. GUARD pure policy remains domain; DispatchHost orchestration is application composition; Tauri UI/commands are driving adapters; EXEC is existing driven boundary.
architecture.A3 Module dependency view: See diagram B. No concrete infrastructure dependency enters GUARD. No new repository, global manager, authentication subsystem or framework.
architecture.A4 Responsibilities: execution-guard: evaluate validated implementation envelope before execution. SPEC owns approved contract revisions; EVID owns classified evidence; WORK owns project/root/lease; CORE owns board task projection. None currently owns trusted task intent or a complete approval binding.
architecture.A5 Input ports: Existing start_run and start_implementation. Proposed reference-only implementation command shape is NOT APPROVED; existing caller-provided boolean is insufficient.
architecture.A6 Output ports: Reuse existing SPEC/EVID/WORK read access and EXEC start path after approved binding design. No new production port proposed at this gate.
architecture.A7 Driving adapters: Tauri commands and desktop UI; future Agent transports must share the same host check. UI presence is not proof a call came from a human.
architecture.A8 Driven adapters: Existing execution adapters; planning uses no process/network/filesystem mutation. Proposed session-local record requires no persistence adapter.
architecture.A9 Dependencies: Tauri -> DispatchHost -> validated domain values -> GUARD policy; DispatchHost -> existing SPEC/EVID/WORK APIs; EXEC reached only after all checks.
architecture.A10 State ownership: Current SPEC and EVID stores remain authoritative only for their existing scopes. Proposed HOST session approval/intent record is a NEW owner requiring approval; not yet implemented. HTML is a projection.
architecture.A11 Mutation boundary: Proposed explicit local-human confirmation creates session record; Agent can reference only, cannot register/reclassify/approve. Host checks identity/freshness every start. Exact capability separation remains an open architecture question.
architecture.A12 Transaction boundary: Read current task/project/fingerprint/revision/evidence -> compare all bindings -> pure GUARD -> existing execution preflight -> start once. Any rejection before start creates zero external side effects. Revalidate before start; atomicity against revision edits must be specified before skeleton.
architecture.A13 External boundary: No new server, network authority or persistent approval store. Session-only proposal excludes hostile local OS user/process security; cannot advertise authenticated human provenance without a concrete protected confirmation mechanism.
architecture.A14 Forbidden dependencies: GUARD -> UI/FS/OS/network; Agent-set approved or behavioral label -> authority; unknown intent -> generic default; contract hash -> full architecture/BDD hash; stale pass -> later unrelated run; direct UI/Agent -> EXEC bypass.

contracts: C1 Implementation start requires a host-resolved, owner-approved, current binding; caller approved/RED fields cannot grant permission.
C2 Generic execution remains available only for tasks explicitly classified generic by the approved trusted flow; unknown intent rejects. No title regex or caller kind bypass.

C3 Binding covers task ID, module, project identity/root, current fingerprint, approved architecture/BDD/skeleton revisions, envelope scope and qualified RED evidence identity. Existing two-field EVID binding alone does not prove this.
C4 Missing/mismatched/revised/revoked/session-expired records reject before EXEC; no prior pass reuse.
C5 Existing pure GUARD scope/protected-path semantics remain; successful policy check is necessary but not sufficient.
C6 No production change until owner chooses authority and classification boundary; no current public API/schema is silently changed.
invariants: I1 No external start before all authority/policy/binding checks.
I2 Agent cannot self-classify or self-approve.
I3 Generic compatibility cannot be used to execute implementation tasks.
I4 Current stores do not silently gain stronger guarantees.
I5 HTML status never implies executable RED/GREEN.

gap: Existing code has no authenticated approval actor/source or authoritative task intent. A local command and in-memory approved flag do not fill the gap. Full binding not representable by existing schemas. Do not invent a new trusted repository or silently reject all generic runs.
risks: Human confirmation capability must be inaccessible to Agent self-approval, otherwise threat model remains unresolved.
Session-only proposal sacrifices restart continuity and does not protect against malicious local OS user.
Binding atomicity with SPEC changes and EXEC preflight requires explicit design before code.
Current fixture-only SPEC loading is not real project approval ingestion.
